image_description: A close-up macro photograph of a brown butterfly, identified as a Ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), perched on green vegetation. The butterfly's wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is dark brown with distinct rows of small, pale-ringed eyespots (ocelli). The body appears fuzzy and brown, matching the wings. One antenna is clearly visible with a clubbed tip. Several legs are visible gripping the plant stem.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral wing surface is dark brown. A row of distinct ocelli with pale centers and rings is clearly visible along the margin of the hindwing and forewing.

The body appears slender relative to the wings and has a visible fuzzy/hairy texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While Ringlets are Nymphalids and have reduced forelegs, they are tucked against the head/thorax and are not clearly distinguishable from the other legs or the body fuzz in this specific angle/resolution.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (three tagmata).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The division between head, thorax, and abdomen is structurally implied and consistent with insect anatomy, though the segmentation is obscured by hair.
